This is a stabilizing factor in the City's economic base. It is generally found to be true that areas with high percentages of governmental employment, (especially State and Federal jobs) tend to be very stable over long periods of time, and that other segments of the local economy benefit from this stability.
Manufacturing, although on a decline in the area, remains an important element in the economic base of the community. A number of these manufacturing concerns located within the employment market of the project are listed in Table 8. Table 8 also indicates the type of product, number of employees and location (the figure for number of Commonwealth employees will not correspond to those in previous tables since it is based on a recent 1972 survey conducted by the Tri-County United Fund/Pennsylvania Bureau of Employment Security).
The rate of unemployment in the Harrisburg area also indicates strong stability in the local economy. A survey, as of May 1972, conducted by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Employment Security indicates an unemployment rate of 2.5 percent for Harrisburg. This figure compares very favorably with that of the 12 other metropolitan areas of the State (See Table 9 below) and with the overall State average of 5.3 percent for the period.
